newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-GERMAN FIRST DIVISION WEEKEND PROGRAMME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMAN FIRST DIVISION WEEKEND PROGRAMME.

text.p: Weekend matches in the German first division:

Bayern Munich (2) v 1860 Munich (9) (kickoff 1700 GMT). Bayern welcome back international defender Thomas Helmer. Will be without midfielder Mario Basler (ankle injury) and wing back Christian Ziege (knee operation). 1860 waiting to see if midfielder Peter Nowak recovers from stomach muscle problem.

Bochum (7) v Hansa Rostock (14). (1900). Promoted Bochum having a good run and unbeaten at home and on four-match winning streak. Hansa need points to get away from the relegation zone and welcome back Andre Hofschneider in defensive midfield role after suspension.

Stuttgart beaten only once this season and must fancy chances at struggling Hamburg club. Leaders should be at full strength if defender Thomas Berthold comes through fitness test on thigh. St. Pauli striker Jens Scharping will probably only start match on bench after leg muscle injury.

Werder Bremen (6) v Hamburg (11). Bremen unbeaten at home scoring 14 and conceding only three while Hamburg have struggled away from home. Bremen without key striker Bruno Labbadia. Hamburg hope to welcome back striker Karsten Baeron after illness.

Schalke (13) v Borussia Dortmund (4). Champions Dortmund must bounce back from 2-1 Champions' League defeat at home by Atletico Madrid in midweek and win points in this derby to have chance of narrowing four-point gap on leaders.
Arminia Bielefeld (18) v Fortuna Duesseldorf (10). Promoted Bielefeld won just once this season and Fortuna have good chance to pick up away points.
Duisburg (16) v Freiburg (17). Bottom-of-the-table clash and nobody expects a classic. Duisburg not expected to make major changes if striker Bachirou Salou makes it after flu.

Bayer Leverkusen (3) v Borussia Moenchengladbach (12). Leverkusen just three points off leaders and expected to be unchanged. Swedish striker Martin Dahlin returns to Bundesliga for Moenchengladbach after unsuccessful time in Italy. Away team also welcome back key playmaker Stefan Effenberg. Moenchengladbach not won away this season but Effenberg and Dahlin comebacks might give them much-needed boost.

Karlsruhe (8) v Cologne (5). Cologne, who been in good form away, hope to have Austrian striker Toni Polster back after groin strain and Rhine club should field strongest team. Karlsruhe hoping to build on their UEFA Cup success against Roma in midweek.
